# Infinitary queue 11. Generated by Infinitary from one source; a newer Infinitary offers its update as a pull request, so change it there, not by hand.
# The shipped fix-forward queue on GitLab (docs/forge.md in Infinitary, "The
# shipped queue on GitLab"). The project's own .gitlab-ci.yml includes this
# file and lists the infinitary-queue stage. An approver's merge click in
# Infinitary marks the approved version with the commit status
# infinitary/queue and starts a pipeline on the default branch through the
# API, the kind of pipeline these jobs run in, with a schedule's (the
# project's own jobs leave the API's out). The form job gathers every change so marked, composes them
# onto the default branch, and the checks job runs the project's batch checks
# (.gitlab/infinitary-batch-checks.yml, the one file of the queue the project
# writes itself) on the composed batch as a child pipeline. The verdict job
# writes the result: green passes every change, then the merge job merges it.
# Red pauses every change behind one issue, reruns nothing and blames no change. A merge request labelled
# infinitary-queue-fix after the pause began ends it once it is approved; a
# resume or a send-back by hand from Infinitary ends it too.
#
# A Maintainer may queue a change without Infinitary by putting the label
# infinitary-queue on it. A label starts no pipeline, so the form job reads
# it when the queue next starts: after a mark, a merge or an answer, or on a
# pipeline schedule the project runs on its default branch, which these jobs
# run in too.
#
# The form, verdict and merge jobs write with the project access token Infinitary
# keeps as INFINITARY_QUEUE_TOKEN: masked, protected, and scoped to the
# infinitary-queue environment, which only the queue jobs name, so nothing
# in a batch receives it.

.infinitary-queue:
  stage: infinitary-queue
  interruptible: false
  rules:
    - if: ($CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule") && $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

# One queue job at a time across pipelines: every form reads the queue again,
# so a start that waits loses nothing.
# The checks job is a trigger job, which GitLab refuses an image, so only
# the jobs that run the queue's script name one.
infinitary-queue-form:
  extends: .infinitary-queue
  image: node:22
  resource_group: infinitary-queue
  environment:
    name: infinitary-queue
    action: prepare
  variables:
    GIT_DEPTH: "0"
  script:
    - node .gitlab/infinitary/gitlab-cli.mjs form
  artifacts:
    paths: [infinitary-batch.yml]
    reports:
      dotenv: infinitary-queue.env
    expire_in: 1 week

# The batch's own code runs in this child pipeline with no queue variable:
# nothing in a batch can mark itself passed. The child includes the project's
# .gitlab/infinitary-batch-checks.yml from the default branch.
infinitary-queue-checks:
  extends: .infinitary-queue
  needs: [infinitary-queue-form]
  trigger:
    include:
      - artifact: infinitary-batch.yml
        job: infinitary-queue-form
    strategy: depend

infinitary-queue-verdict:
  extends: .infinitary-queue
  image: node:22
  resource_group: infinitary-queue
  environment:
    name: infinitary-queue
    action: prepare
  needs:
    - job: infinitary-queue-form
      artifacts: true
    - job: infinitary-queue-checks
  variables:
    GIT_DEPTH: "1"
  rules:
    - if: ($CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule") && $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
      when: always
  script:
    - node .gitlab/infinitary/gitlab-cli.mjs decide

# Only trusted queue instructions run here; the batch child never receives this environment's key.
infinitary-queue-merge:
  extends: .infinitary-queue
  image: node:22
  resource_group: infinitary-queue
  environment:
    name: infinitary-queue
    action: prepare
  needs:
    - job: infinitary-queue-verdict
  rules:
    - if: ($CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule") && $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
      when: always
  script:
    - node .gitlab/infinitary/gitlab-cli.mjs merge
